# Power and cost tables (generated by power_cost.py)

## Power for the full-model interaction I (5 cells, optimal allocation 2:1:1:1:1)

sigma = seed sd of log val loss. The task's assumption is sd 0.004 in loss; at a cell loss of L that is sigma = 0.004/L (0.004 at L=1.0, 0.0067 at L=0.6). Runs needed N for 80% power (alpha 0.05, two-sided); per-cell n in brackets (000 gets double).

| sigma | delta 1.0% | delta 1.5% | delta 2.0% | delta 3.0% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.003 | 26 (5/10) | 12 (2/4) | 7 (2/4) | 3 (1/2) |
| 0.004 | 46 (8/16) | 21 (4/8) | 12 (2/4) | 6 (1/2) |
| 0.005 | 71 (12/24) | 32 (6/12) | 18 (3/6) | 8 (2/4) |
| 0.0067 | 127 (22/44) | 57 (10/20) | 32 (6/12) | 15 (3/6) |
| 0.01 | 283 (48/96) | 126 (21/42) | 71 (12/24) | 32 (6/12) |

MDE (log units, 80% power) at fixed N, sigma 0.004: N=10: 2.13%, N=20: 1.50%, N=30: 1.23%, N=48: 0.97%, N=60: 0.87%, N=90: 0.71%
If seeds share the data order (common random numbers) with within-pair correlation rho between cells, Var scales by (1-rho): rho 0.3 cuts N by 30%. Not assumed; measured in the pilot.

## E1 decomposition cost (20M tokens, deduplicated set)

- Minimal tier (the outside review's version): 9 arms + E1 control, seed 0, LR 6e-3 = 10 runs = **0.55 GPU-h** (33 min). Reads only effects larger than about 2 x sqrt(2) x sigma (1.1% at sigma .004).
- Rigorous tier: each arm and the E1 and E10 controls get LR {3e-3, 6e-3} at seed 0 (equal tuning budget), then 2 more seeds at the better LR: 11 x 4 = 44 runs = **2.41 GPU-h**. Arm-vs-control SE = 0.004 x sqrt(1/3+1/3) = 0.33% (MDE 80% power = 0.92%).
